To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• Parallel DBMSs are better at executing tasks that require multiple joins and/or multiple scans of the same data, while MR systems are better at executing single-scan tasks, especially those with large data volumes.
the MapReduce paradigm is not a dramatically new computing paradigm and that it is not a good choice when high performance is required.

(i) MR is a useful paradigm for data-intensive computing that is complementary to parallel DBMSs; (ii) parallel DBMSs are much faster than MR, but are harder to develop; (iii) the performance of parallel DBMS systems is highly dependent on the tuning of the execution plans; (iv) the performance of the MR system is highly dependent on data locality; (v) both systems have a long way to go in terms of scalability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: • What is the best approach to building large-scale data analysis systems?
the question of whether a DBMS or MR system is better suited for a particular task.
the following two questions: (1) What are the differences between MR and parallel DBMSs? and (2) Which one should be used to solve a given problem?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both approaches are valid and that there are situations where one or the other will be preferable.
both paradigms have their advantages and disadvantages.
MR systems are not a new paradigm but a new implementation of a well-known paradigm, namely parallel DBMSs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MR is a very good choice for a quick-and-dirty prototype, but that a parallel DBMS is a better choice for production use.
the MR paradigm has some advantages, but the performance and ease-of-use of parallel DBMS systems are still much better.
MR is not the new paradigm, but it is a new implementation concept for parallel DBMSs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MR model, while useful in many situations, is not the only approach to large-scale data processing.
, while there is no single best way to process large-scale data, it is important to understand the tradeoffs and the performance of different systems.
the MR paradigm is not a dramatically new model of computation, but rather a reimplementation of a model that has existed for over 20 years.
